title: All-Hands: Q2 Results
description: Company-wide update on Q2 performance and Q3 priorities.
_comment: extra_participants exist as attendees without accounts — an all-hands is exactly where that happens, and it takes this meeting past twenty for the avatar-overflow case (T05-F).
transcript: Afternoon everyone. Thanks for making the time — I know it's late in the day for the European folks.
I want to do this differently from last quarter. Less slides, more actual detail, and I'll take questions properly at the end rather than pretending we're out of time.
So. Q2. The headline is that we grew, and that the growth was less even than the number suggests.
Revenue was up twenty-two percent quarter on quarter. That's ahead of the plan we set in March.
But almost all of it came from expansion in existing accounts, not new logos.
New business was roughly flat. If you're on the sales team, you already knew that.
I don't want to spin that as a good thing. Expansion is healthy — it means the product works for people who use it — but flat new business is a real signal.
Sarah, do you want to take the product side of that?
Sure. I think the honest read is that our product is easy to expand and hard to start.
Once a team is using it, other teams see the output and adopt. That's why expansion works.
But the first-run experience is genuinely poor, particularly on mobile, and that shows up as flat new business.
We lose about forty percent of mobile signups partway through. That's not a subtle number.
And that's why mobile onboarding is a Q3 priority rather than a nice-to-have.
Correct. It's the single change with the clearest line to new business.
Let me go through the other numbers before we get into Q3.
Net revenue retention was a hundred and eighteen percent. That's genuinely strong and it's the number I'd point an investor at.
Gross churn was four point one percent, which is up slightly from three point six.
The increase is two accounts, both of which were acquired and consolidated onto a competitor's contract. That's not a product failure but it does count against us.
Headcount is fifty-four, up from forty-nine. Four of those five were engineering.
Support ticket volume per customer is down eleven percent, which I want to call out because it's the result of deliberate work by Yuki's team.
That's the kind of number that doesn't get celebrated because nothing visible happened.
Right. Q3 priorities. There are three, and I want to be clear that there are only three.
One: mobile onboarding. Sarah covered why.
Two: usage-based pricing for the enterprise tier.
This one's going to generate questions so let me pre-empt the main one — no, this is not a price rise dressed up as a model change.
Some customers will pay more. Some will pay less. The ones who'll pay more are the ones currently using four times the median volume on the same seat price.
Existing contracts are grandfathered for two quarters and everyone gets sixty days' notice. Nobody finds out from an invoice.
Three: reliability. Specifically, putting configuration changes behind the same review process as code.
We had two incidents this quarter with the same root cause. That's not bad luck, that's a missing process, and we're funding the fix.
Can I add something to that?
The thing I'd want people to take away is that reliability made the list at all.
It's competing with two revenue-facing projects and it won. That's a deliberate choice and it should tell you something about how we're prioritising.
What's not on the list — and I want to be explicit because people will ask — is the analytics rebuild, the Salesforce integration, and the self-serve tier.
All three are reasonable. None of them are happening this quarter. If you're working on one of them, come and talk to me.
Okay, questions. I'll take them in the order they came in on the channel.
First one — 'Does flat new business mean we're pausing hiring in sales?'
No. We're not pausing, but we're not accelerating either. Two open roles stay open, and I'm not adding a third until onboarding lands.
Second — 'How confident are we in the mobile onboarding date?'
Moderately. It's slipped twice, which I'm not going to hide.
The difference this time is that we've identified the specific technical risk — deep-link handling — and we're spiking it before committing rather than after.
So I'd say the date is more likely to hold than the last two, but I won't say it's certain.
That's the right level of confidence to express publicly.
Third question — 'Will usage-based pricing affect the team's commission structure?'
Yes, and we haven't finished working out how. I'd rather say that than invent an answer.
What I'll commit to is that nobody's commission gets restructured without a conversation first, and that no change lands mid-quarter.
Fourth — and this is the last one on the list — 'Are we profitable?'
Not yet. We're closer than we were. At current burn and current growth we've got runway into the second half of next year.
That's not a crisis and it's not comfortable either. It's why the three priorities are the three priorities.
One thing I'd add — if you're unclear how your work connects to one of those three, that's a reasonable thing to ask your lead, and it's a fair question.
Agreed. And if the honest answer is that it doesn't connect, that's worth surfacing too.
Okay. Thanks everyone. Slides and the recording go out this evening.
And genuinely — thank you for the support-volume number. That one was hard-won.

summary.overview: Q2 revenue grew 22% quarter on quarter and net revenue retention reached 118%, but essentially all growth came from expansion in existing accounts while new business was flat. Sarah attributed this to a product that is easy to expand and hard to start, with roughly forty percent of mobile signups abandoning partway through. Q3 has exactly three priorities — mobile onboarding, usage-based enterprise pricing, and putting configuration changes behind review — with the analytics rebuild, Salesforce integration and self-serve tier explicitly excluded. Raj confirmed the company is not yet profitable, with runway into the second half of next year.
summary.gist: Growth is all expansion; three Q3 priorities named, three initiatives explicitly cut.

outline.title: What is not on the list

bullets: Revenue up 22% quarter on quarter, ahead of the March plan.
Almost entirely expansion in existing accounts; new business roughly flat.
Net revenue retention 118%; gross churn 4.1%, up from 3.6% on two acquisition-driven losses.
The product is easy to expand and hard to start.
~40% of mobile signups abandon partway through — the clearest line to new business.
Support tickets per customer down 11% through deliberate work, called out as invisible progress.
Explicitly not a price rise dressed as a model change — some accounts pay less.
Targets accounts using ~4× median volume at the same seat price.
Two quarters of grandfathering and sixty days' notice; nobody learns of it from an invoice.

Commission impact of usage-based pricing unresolved; no restructure without a conversation and none mid-quarter.
Not yet profitable; runway into the second half of next year.
